correctness.rationale: Unique a/b gap factorization; a b^t a occurs exactly when >=t interior b letters; Gaussian complete-homogeneous enumeration with fixed trailing count yields coefficient polynomial. For A>C and B>=C, forced zero trailing b gives restricted partitions. The unrestricted denominator is a Gaussian rectangle partition count; a pole-order argument and Hardy–Ramanujan give the sharp asymptotic. Independent direct finite word enumeration matched 252 parameter triples, 3354 coefficients, 320 chamber instances. Infinite validity comes from proof, not tests.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The established unrestricted Parikh-class partition theorem counts all words; it does not distinguish avoidance of the specified long scattered pattern. A generic algorithm to count subsequences is not the same as an exact parametric evaluation or sharp asymptotic.

value.rationale: The recent fixed-Parikh-matrix literature asks quantitative fixed-pattern probabilities. The theorem evaluates an entire natural long-palindromic-scattered-pattern family exactly for all fixed counts, isolates a large stable region, and gives a sharp asymptotic constant. It is structurally stronger than unconstrained Gaussian class enumeration or isolated small cases, furnishing an analytic benchmark for broader word-pattern distributions.
